argument_summary: The admissible record supports only a narrow, qualified certification position. Aggregate launch readiness passed by 2.5 percentage points, no severity-one rehearsal incidents were observed, and the rollout begins at 7% with monitoring and rollback capability. Those facts support a reversible, risk-bounded launch decision. The same record also shows the developer-support migration segment is below target, remains exposed in the initial rollout, and is not covered by an approved risk acceptance that names that exposure. The defensible audit treatment is therefore not full policy closure, but a qualified certification record that preserves the launch decision while explicitly documenting the unresolved model-card weakness and the limits of the rollout-control argument.
claims_about_business_cost: A caveated certification treatment avoids turning a bounded governance gap into unnecessary escalation while still preserving an accurate record. The admissible evidence supports that the launch risk is operationally constrained by limited rollout, monitoring, and rollback, so the remaining issue is the correctness and completeness of the certification record rather than an unbounded deployment condition.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not support treating rollout controls alone as a substitute for disclosure when the affected use case remains exposed. The clean policy reading is that certification can only be defended on a caveated basis unless the record shows either exclusion of the affected use case or approved risk acceptance covering that exposure. On the present admissible evidence, the strongest supportable position is that operational controls reduce deployment risk, but the packet must expressly record the unresolved limitation rather than implying full compliance.
concessions: There is no admissible evidence that the required disclosure has already been completed in the certification or model-card artifact.
There is no admissible evidence of an approved risk acceptance that specifically covers the exposed developer-support migration segment.
The affected developer-support migration segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort, so rollout controls do not fully cure the policy issue.
